chapter_title: The Seventh, concerning the Five Fathers
chapter_note: The first half is dominated by an ordered, impersonal emanation-schema (Father → three emanations → further triads), characteristic of the systematic cosmological teaching layer. The second half shows clear editorial fatigue: institutional identifications (apostles/church), explicit elect/catechumen address (seam-flagged), and a Gospel-style citation/paraphrase (Jn 8) embedded in the third-power description.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Hagiographic/dialogue frame: "enlightener…apostle…disciples…revelation" situates a speaker and audience rather than expounding cosmological structure.

paragraphs.core_text: Five fathers exist; they were summoned forth one of one. [Also], one did come out of another!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Programmatic, numbered cosmological schema stated impersonally (emanation chain).

paragraphs.core_text: The first Father is the Father of Greatness, the blessed one of glory, the [on]e who has no measure to his greatness; who also is the first only-begotten, the first eternal; who exists with fiv[e fa]thers for ever; the one who exists before every thing that has existed, and that will exist.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic definition of the highest divinity in timeless, superlative terms; no institutional anchoring.

paragraphs.core_text: Now he, the glorious Father, summoned from him three emanations. The [fi]rst is the Gre[at] Spirit, the first Mother, who came out of the Father. She appeared first.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Emanation mechanics in ordered triad form (core taxonomic voice).

paragraphs.core_text: The seco[nd i]s the Belo[ved of] the Lights, the great glorious Beloved, [the one w]ho is honour[ed; w]ho came out of the Father. [He ma]nifested ou[t of h]im.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the triadic emanation list; “honoured” raises application-voice score but remains internal to the cosmological genealogy.

paragraphs.core_text: The third father is the Thir[d Ambassador], the eldest of [a]]] the counsell[ors; who came out of] the first Father. He appeared.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the triad from the Father; impersonal listing of hypostases.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the first Father, the first power, the one from whom the three great powers came out. This is the first Father, the first eternal, the root of all the lights; from whom the three emanations came out. They have humiliated the Darkness. They have brought its heart's desire to naught. They have given themselves the victory. They have also given the victory to their aeons.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic process/outcome language (victory over personified Darkness; aeons) remains wholly within the mythic-cosmological system.

paragraphs.core_text: The second father, who came out of the first Father, is the Third Ambassador, the model of the King of lights. And again, he too summoned and sent out of him three powers.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Iterative structural pattern: father → three powers (systematic cosmological recursion).

paragraphs.core_text: One is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man; the one who bears up under all things; the great Pillar of blessing; the great porter, who is greater than all the porters.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmological hypostasis described by function/titles; no church/institutional identification.

paragraphs.core_text: The second is glorious Jesus the Splendour; [the] one through whom shall be given life eternal.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Jesus the Splendour appears as a named cosmic power within a triad (core-compatible), though the phrasing “life eternal” could reflect later Christianized diction (uncertain).

paragraphs.core_text: The third is the Virgin of Light, the glorious wisd[o]m; the one who takes away the heart of the [rul]ers and the powers by her image, as she fulfils the pleas[u]re of the greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic-cosmic agency (rulers/powers as cosmic authorities) in impersonal explanatory voice.

paragraphs.core_text: The third father, who came out of the second father: he is glorious Jesus the Splendour. And, again, he too summoned three evocations after the pattern of the second father.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the emanation recursion (“after the pattern”); still internal taxonomy, not institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: The first power whom he summoned is the Light Min[d].
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed institutional/application identification: “father of all the apostles, the eldest of [a]ll the [ch]urches; … appointed … in the holy church” (cosmos→contemporary church mapping; “apostles/church” are later ecclesial terms).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens as a cosmological triad member, then pivots to church legitimation language (“holy church”, “apostles”, “our pattern”).

paragraphs.core_text: The second power whom Jesus summo[n]ed is the gre[at Jud]ge, who gives judgement on all the souls of mankind, [his] dwelling being established in the atmosphere under [ ... / ... ] wheel [ ... ] stars.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic-judicial function located in cosmological geography (atmosphere/wheel/stars); no institutional address.

paragraphs.core_text: The third power is [the Y]outh, the gre[at ... ] light in his two persons, in [ ... ], I am speaking about that which has been established in the summons [and] the obedience.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed Gospel/NT-style material (Jn 8 paraphrase): “... what I have seen with my Father, [I tell to] you … do that.” Also removed associated “saviour” citation framing as later Christian overlay.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Begins with cosmological identification of a power (Youth) but then inserts a recognizably Johannine saying (NT entry vector).

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth father is the Light Mind. And, again, he too summoned three powers after the pattern of Jesus.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed institutional clause: “the one who chooses all the churches” (cosmos→church mapping).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Structural continuation of the father/triad pattern, with an added ecclesial gloss on “churches” likely from a later hand.
Institutional/mission language centered on “Apostle of Light” and “church of the flesh…humanity”; not impersonal cosmological mapping.
Hagiographic-institutional accompaniment motif (“counterpart…to the apostle…help…dangers”) rather than cosmological system exposition.
Seam-flagged institutional extension: elect/catechumens and renunciation requirement anchor to community discipline.

paragraphs.core_text: And also the fifth father is this Light Form; the one who shall appear to everyone who will go out from his body; and the thr[ee] great glorious angels who are come with her.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed institutional/legitimating clause: “corresponding to the pattern of the image to the apostle” (ties cosmic appearance to apostolic/church authority).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core eschatological-cosmological appearance teaching with a later apostolic ‘pattern’ gloss appended.
Seam-flagged paragraph: although it lists angelic insignia, it culminates in an explicit institutional destinatary (“elect and the catechumens”), marking a late ecclesial application/extension.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the five fathers who have come out of one another. They have appeared and man[ifes]ted through one another!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Formal closure of the emanation chain in impersonal summary (system-complete statement).
Homiletic beatitude/exhortation (“Blessed is he…doers of good things”) oriented to moral identity and reward rather than cosmological mechanics.
